The examples use the Western Collaborative Group Study, which followed 3154 middle-aged men for coronary heart disease [@rosenman1975coronary].
In `data/wcgs.csv`, the outcome `chd` is 1 for a man with an incident case and 0 for a man without one.
The feature is his body mass index, `bmi`.
Each plot also shows the line fitted to `chd` by least squares on `bmi`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
wcgs <- read.csv("data/wcgs.csv")
fit_bmi <- lm(chd ~ bmi, data = wcgs)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

wcgs = pd.read_csv("data/wcgs.csv")
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(wcgs["bmi"], wcgs["chd"], 1)
fitted_bmi = intercept + slope * wcgs["bmi"]
```

:::
